work_orders.brief: Present the anchor: a monarch butterfly fluttering near a milkweed plant, landing on a leaf to lay a tiny egg. Ask what the learner thinks that egg will become. Do not name any stages yet.
work_orders.evidence: The anchor is a single observable event that begins the monarch life cycle, and the orient slot needs a concrete situation, not an explanation.

work_orders.brief: Quickly call up what the learner already knows: butterflies are insects, insects hatch from eggs, and a butterfly is the adult form that flies. Do not explain life cycle yet.
work_orders.evidence: The learner already holds three facts that can be linked into the new idea, and the orient slot needs to surface those prerequisites briefly.

work_orders.brief: Identify the four main stages in the monarch life cycle: egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly. For each stage, say what the organism is doing in that stage: the egg holds the young, the caterpillar eats and grows, the chrysalis shelters the change, and the butterfly is the adult that can fly and lay eggs. Do not yet state that the series repeats.
work_orders.evidence: The objective names a series of stages, and the anchor provides the concrete monarch example through which each stage can be named.

work_orders.brief: Define a life cycle as the series of stages an organism passes through from egg to adult, and state that a butterfly's life cycle repeats when an adult butterfly produces young that grow into new adults. Use the monarch from the anchor as the example organism.
work_orders.evidence: The objective requires the learner to state that a life cycle is a series of stages that repeats when adults produce young, and the anchor gives the concrete organism for that definition.

work_orders.brief: Surface the wrong belief that the egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, and butterfly are four different kinds of animals. Ask the learner to decide whether the four stages in the anchor are the same organism at different times or four separate organisms. Do not explain the correct answer in the same breath as the question.
work_orders.evidence: The approved misconception says students treat the stages as four unrelated animals, and the contrast slot must test that wrong model against the anchor rather than restate it.

work_orders.brief: Surface the wrong belief that the life cycle only goes forward and then stops. Ask the learner to decide what must happen for a new egg to appear on a milkweed leaf. Do not yet state that the butterfly must lay the egg.
work_orders.evidence: The approved misconception says students see the cycle as a line that ends at butterfly, and the contrast slot must test whether the learner can identify the missing return step.

work_orders.brief: Contrast a life cycle with a line that stops. Name a line that stops as one that goes egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly, then nothing. Then name a life cycle as the same four stages but with the butterfly producing a new egg. Do not introduce a new organism.
work_orders.evidence: The objective asks for the idea that the cycle repeats, and the contrast slot needs a side-by-side comparison that separates the wrong linear model from the correct repeating one.

work_orders.brief: Ask the learner to identify what an adult butterfly must do for the life cycle to continue.
work_orders.evidence: Objective requires reconstructing an ordered sequence; attach a Sequence interaction so the learner can respond.
